subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add editable workspace-wide file management and/or host system filesystem browsing beyond the current read-only workspace API, and what permission boundary should replace or sit beside the allowlisted `agents.files.*` editor?
rationale: This changes which files operator clients can read or mutate through Gateway/UI surfaces and crosses a boundary that was deliberately tightened after an arbitrary workspace-read security bug.

options.title: Approve workspace mutations only
options.body: Evolve the open workspace-management design into bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutations under explicit admin scopes, keeping host system files out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep read-only workspace browsing
options.body: Leave current main's read-only list/get API plus the allowlisted bootstrap editor as the supported boundary until stronger demand or security design exists.

options.title: Start a separate system-scope design
options.body: Treat host filesystem browsing as a distinct security-reviewed feature with explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX before any implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace mutations only
recommendation.body: Evolve the open workspace-management design into bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutations under explicit admin scopes, keeping host system files out of scope for now.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace API and adjacent UI/app implementations, making them the clearest routing point for the remaining product/security choice.
